Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details a highly technical media buying strategy for Black Friday, emphasizing marginal contribution margin scaling, delayed attribution modeling (1-day vs. 30-day click gaps), and pre-season spend allocation rules to build retargeting funnels prior to CPM spikes. modules: [ADC] topics: [campaign setup and tracking, scaling, attribution and modeling] tier: 2 scope_hint: core

Topics. campaign setup and tracking / Establishing the technical groundwork for Black Friday media buying by configuring pacing sheets with 3-day rolling marginal averages and utilizing multiple attribution windows (e.g., 7-day click and 1-day engaged) to compensate for platform lag. Preparing Google Ads infrastructure by updating Merchant Center feeds, implementing promotional pricing lines, and adjusting Search/PMax campaigns well in advance to capture demand during peak CPM spikes. Building out an "offer ladder"—a pre-loaded hierarchy of fallback promotions (e.g., deeper discounts, gift-with-purchase)—that can be deployed rapidly intraday if baseline contribution margins stall. scaling / Executing budget deployment strategies that prioritize marginal returns over blended averages, scaling ad spend strictly until "contribution margin 3" flatlines (the point where marginal ROAS equals break-even ROAS). Transitioning from top-of-funnel awareness buying in October to bottom-of-funnel harvesting during the Black Friday weekend. Utilizing "cost cap" campaigns selectively to map the marginal frontier and gauge elasticity before pushing volume through standard maximize volume campaigns. attribution and modeling / Adjusting ROAS expectations by recognizing that ad spend in the weeks leading up to Black Friday acts as a lagging indicator; a seemingly poor 1.0 ROAS on a 30-day click model often backdates to a highly profitable 4.0 ROAS once the sale triggers delayed conversions. Using hold-out experiments to measure post-treatment lift (the causal halo effect of pre-spend) to justify allocating up to 31–43% of the Q4 budget into September and October. Recalculating Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) tolerances by adjusting for lower gross margins during sales and factoring in historically weaker 6-month repeat purchase rates (LTV) for November cohorts compared to evergreen cohorts.

Look for. The definition of the 30-day vs. 1-day click gap: the phenomenon where pre-sale ad spend shows poor immediate ROAS but drives high deferred revenue when the sale goes live. The metric used to dictate when to stop scaling spend: when the marginal "contribution margin 3" (CM3) starts to flatten out. The definition of a post-treatment lift: the incremental value that appears after a hold-out test concludes, demonstrating the delayed effect of early ad spend. The percentage of Q4 budget recommended for September and October: 31% to 43%.

Skip. General macroeconomic updates regarding the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) interest rate hikes or broad inflation statistics. Broad guidelines on creative diversity or establishing the "CAST" framework (Conceit, Actor, Style, Terrain, Setup) for video ads.
